objective: 0.3.1: assess pi-codex-conversion as a Codex provider for Pi, in particular whether it supports Codex's new context_management system, gpt-reserve, auto-review/auto-approve and comparable Codex features.
requirements: Maintainer (verbatim, 2026-11-09): "alright for 0.3.1 let's first assess a codex provider for pi", "I'd like to know whether pi-codex-conversion does context_management (the new system), gpt-reserve, auto-review/auto-approve, etc".
This is an assessment only: deliver findings and stop; build nothing until the maintainer says to go ahead.
Testing rules carried from 0.3.0: never run pi or make live model requests; read sources only.

Maintainer (verbatim, 2026-11-09): "didn't we agree on using just-bash as the bash tool backend", "we should also support the just-bash's ts/js capabilities (ts as first option, js as fallback)". No earlier record of that choice was found in the original request, the repository, its issues or the Intents.

Decided (maintainer, 2026-11-09, after research showed just-bash 3.6.0 is a simulated shell that cannot run host executables): "use just-bash and allow the executables on PATH and other relevant places (cross-platform)". The Pi bash tool runs on just-bash (through Pi 1.5.0 BashOperations); commands it does not implement resolve to real executables on PATH and other relevant locations, on Linux, macOS and Windows, so git, bun, bunx, mise, gh, node and the holyagent CLI keep working; just-bash TypeScript execution is offered first and JavaScript is the fallback.

Codex provider finding: @howaboua/pi-codex-conversion tools.applyPatchOnly keeps Pi read, bash, edit and write plus apply_patch, but turns off its native V2 compaction and Codex prompt while its own Codex provider stays registered (assignment-0mw96dgh6-ud60).

Decided (maintainer, verbatim, 2026-11-09): "about the shadowed commands, prefer them instead of the ones in PATH". Where just-bash implements a command itself (rg, grep, sed, find, tar, diff, awk, jq, ls, xargs and the rest), its built-in runs, and the host executable of the same name is not registered; only commands just-bash lacks pass through to the host.

Maintainer (verbatim, 2026-11-09): "btw the new codex provider should have auto review and context_management". The Codex provider HolyAgent ships has Codex auto-review (tool calls reviewed by the codex-auto-review reviewer) and context_management (Codex server-side compaction) while keeping apply_patch plus the just-bash bash and Pi read, edit and write; pi-codex-conversion applyPatchOnly mode turns native compaction off, so the plan must provide both another way.

Maintainer (verbatim, 2026-11-09): "and also, we have the fff integration right? as well as billion context?", "if we don't have billion context and fff the agent I asked to record the stuff in the docs and intents was incredibly terible". Found: Billion Context is shipped (pin 0.1.212, docs/pi/caching-and-subagents.md). fff was dropped by a recorded decision of 2026-10-27 (intent-0mvqtcahb-ipze: "drop fff; bundle ripgrep and fd in the plugin") for the Claude plugin search, and was never carried into the Pi work. just-bash has no record in any Intent, branch or doc.

Default (root judgement, revisitable): the Pi integration adds @ff-labs/pi-fff (0.11.0, MIT, in-process fff Node binding) at an exact pin in override mode, so its tools replace Pi find and grep and Pi prompt guidance stays consistent; the Claude plugin keeps the bundled ripgrep and fd from the 2026-10-27 decision.

Conflict found (assignment-0mw96qjlf-o4zi): Billion Context cancels Pi compaction and rewrites outgoing requests, openai-codex-responses included, so it clashes with Codex context_management (server-side compaction with an encrypted item replayed); its bash guardrails (60 s default timeout, 50 KB output cap) also apply to the just-bash bash tool by name.

Decided (maintainer, verbatim, 2026-11-09): "btw billion context probably conflicts with context management, if they don't work similarly prefer billion, if they do prefer context management". They work differently: Billion Context compresses the history client-side through its proxy and keeps it retrievable (compress, decompress, search_context tools), while Codex context_management replaces the history with an opaque encrypted server-side compaction item that cannot be searched or expanded. So Billion Context is preferred: while it is on (pi.features.contextCompression, the default) the Codex provider sends no context_management, and context_management is used only when Billion Context is off.

Maintainer (verbatim, 2026-11-09): "start the spike", "also, billion context's bash safeguards should be turned off if possible". The just-bash spike starts now. Billion Context tool guardrails on the bash tool (default timeout, output cap, repeat detection) are turned off by HolyAgent where Billion Context offers a setting for it; where it does not, the plan says so.

Default (root judgement): the spike runs locally on Linux in a scratch folder outside the repository and is not pushed, because a pushed branch runs the dev pre-release workflow and 0.3.1 has no release branch until 0.3.0 reaches main; Windows and macOS are verified in CI once the 0.3.1 branch exists.

Maintainer (verbatim, 2026-11-09): "also the codex-auto-review should work similarly to how codex's work". Auto-review follows Codex's own auto-review behaviour (what triggers a review, what the reviewer sees, how allow, deny and failure are handled), not a rule list the user must write.

Maintainer (verbatim, 2026-11-09): "also come up with the model routing: use gpt 6.1 sol high for root and come up with the specialist routing using gpt 6.1 terra low->xhigh and gpt 6 luna low-high (xhigh is not good here)", "prefer gpt 6.1 terra for visual stuff and computer use". The Codex route table runs the root on GPT-6.1 Sol at high effort; specialists use GPT-6.1 Terra (low to xhigh) or GPT-6 Luna (low to high, never xhigh); visual work and computer use run on Terra.

Default (root judgement from assignment-0mw96z5n3-mw6f, revisitable): auto-review reproduces Codex guardian behaviour under Pi. Triggers: Pi has no sandbox, so a classifier stands in for escalation: bash commands outside a read-only safe set, writes outside the project root, network use, and tools whose annotations need approval go to review; everything else runs. Request: model codex-auto-review, Codex policy template plus policy text (replaceable or extendable by config), a budgeted transcript (Codex caps: 10k message and 10k tool tokens, last 40 entries) labelled untrusted, the action as JSON, strict GuardianAssessment schema (risk_level, user_authorization, outcome, rationale), 90 s timeout. Decisions: allow runs; deny returns Codex rejection text and instructions to the model; timeout is not a denial and allows one retry; failures deny closed; a breaker stops the turn after 3 consecutive or 10 total denials; a one-retry user override like /approve.

Maintainer (verbatim, 2026-11-09): "also computer use shouldn't be a role, or should it? it would need to cover computer use, browser use (via opencode browse, 0.3.1 should integrate it), and in-app browser". 0.3.1 integrates opencode browse for browser use. Default (root judgement, revisitable): computer use is not a role but a screen capability an Assignment can carry; it grants the specialist the computer-use tools (pi-computer-use), browser use (opencode browse) and the in-app browser (T3 preview tools where T3 hosts the session), and routes that Assignment to GPT-6.1 Terra whatever its role.

Approved (maintainer, verbatim, 2026-11-09: "everything is okay except for this last doubt I had"): Codex route table. Root GPT-6.1 Sol high. GPT-6 Luna: Explorer.map, Explorer.lookup, Librarian.lookup, Worker.validation low; Worker.mechanical, Worker.operations medium; Reviewer.audit high. GPT-6.1 Terra: Explorer.trace, Librarian.research, Worker.integration, Reviewer.testing, Reviewer.artifact medium; Worker.implementation, Reviewer.code, Worker.visual, Reviewer.visual high; Worker.debugging, Reviewer.security xhigh. An Assignment that uses the screen capability runs on Terra at least medium. The auto-review reviewer uses codex-auto-review. Approved too: the auto-review design, the just-bash plan and the Codex provider plan as stated.

Default (root judgement from assignment-0mw9791e9-vhdm, revisitable): opencode browse is @opencode/browse (anomalyco/browse, MIT, 0.0.15, a stdio MCP server plus a paired Chromium extension driving the user's real browser). HolyAgent registers it as an MCP server for Pi at an exact pin, moved by deps:update, and setup reports when the extension is not installed or paired. Screen capability split: pi-computer-use for desktop apps and native browser chrome; browse for web page content in a real browser (sessions, handoff, HAR, recording); T3 preview and HTML render tools for the page shown in T3. Cloud and headless Linux use of browse is unverified and gets its own check in the spike phase.

Maintainer (verbatim, 2026-11-09): "everything is okay then" (approves the screen-capability answer: not a role, a capability carrying computer use, opencode browse and the T3 in-app browser, routed to Terra), and "also, in the same way holycodex 0.16.12 has capabilities, we should. most should be default enabled". HolyAgent gains a capability system modelled on holycodex v0.16.12, with most capabilities enabled by default; the screen capability is one of them.

Maintainer (verbatim, 2026-11-09): "everything should be modular and easily upgradeable btw". Each 0.3.1 piece (just-bash backend, host passthrough, TS/JS execution, Codex provider, auto-review, context_management, fff, opencode browse, the screen capability and the capability system) is its own module behind a narrow interface, can be turned off on its own, and every third-party package or binary it uses sits at an exact pin moved only through mise run deps:update, so upgrading one never requires editing the others.

Maintainer (verbatim, 2026-11-09): "continue until mergeable or blocked", "btw we shall support both headless use and normal use, that's the point of capabilities, to modularly support systems". Capabilities are the module system: each declares what it needs from the system (a display, a desktop session, a paired browser, a network, an OS) and has a headless and a normal form where both make sense (for example the screen capability uses a headless Playwright Chromium in a cloud or CI session and the paired real browser and desktop computer use on a desktop); setup and doctor detect the system and pick the form, and a capability whose needs are missing is reported, not silently dropped.

Default (root judgement from assignment-0mw97bk3l-ykkf, revisitable): a capability registry like holycodex v0.16.12 CAPABILITY_REGISTRY (name, packages and MCP servers, skills and instruction sentences, applicability to root or specialists, default, system needs, doctor health check), driving the existing pi.features switches; toggles through config, setup flags and the setup TUI; doctor reports each selected capability as healthy, missing, disabled or uncertain. Defaults on: core (processes, todo, ask, subagents; required), design and security skills (required), web, context-compression (Billion Context), fff search, code execution (just-bash TS/JS), computer use, browser use (opencode browse), in-app browser (host-managed under T3), auto-review and Luna Reserve (Codex provider only). Default off: session audit. The screen capabilities are granted per Assignment to keep specialist tool lists small.

Maintainer (verbatim, 2026-11-09): "also that means we need gpt 6/gpt 6.1 model guides and instruction sets". 0.3.1 adds a GPT-6/GPT-6.1 model family to packages/runtime/src/instructions: a guide.md drawn from OpenAI's own prompting guidance for those models and Codex's own prompts, and a full instruction set translated from the requirements tree per that guide with the coverage table updated, following the repository requirements skill; the Codex route uses it for the root (Sol) and the specialists (Terra, Luna).

Default (root judgement from spike assignment-0mw96w93p-53j2, revisitable): the just-bash backend runs each shell in a Bun Worker so cancel and Pi's timeout terminate it even in a pure shell loop; it mounts an in-memory /usr/bin and /bin of stubs for host passthrough with the shell PATH set to those and the real PATH given to child processes only; it sets defenseInDepth excludeViolationTypes finalization_registry so ReadWriteFs writes work under Bun; it raises the command, loop, work-unit and js timeout limits; it saves cwd and env even when the command runs exit; it offers host-<name> aliases for host programs a built-in shadows; Windows maps a mount per drive. Billion Context guardrails are turned off by setting BILI_GUARDRAIL_BASH_TIMEOUT=0, BILI_GUARDRAIL_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES=0 and BILI_GUARDRAIL_REPETITION=0 for the Pi process.
